name: Isle of Man
summary_text: Isle of Man stands as a self-legislating Crown Dependency of the United Kingdom with its own parliament, Tynwald. Gender recognition, equality and marriage questions are decided under Manx statutes rather than by automatic application of United Kingdom statutes.  Transgender persons may change legal gender and obtain recognition of the new gender under the Gender Recognition Act 2009 (c.11).  The Equality Act 2017 lists gender reassignment as a protected characteristic and ground of non-discrimination alongside age, disability, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation. The Act was largely in force from 1 January 2019.  A ban covering sexual orientation and gender identity conversion therapy was passed in 2020 as an amendment to the sexual offences bill in the Legislative Council and came into effect in 2024.  Same-sex marriage became effective on 22 July 2016 following Royal Assent on 19 July 2016 to the Marriage and Civil Partnership Act. Civil partnerships have been available since 6 April 2011 and could be converted into marriage without a second ceremony, with the first conversion completed within days of entry into force through routine registration.  Tynwald Hansard for 26 April 2016 records the Legislative Council Third Reading of the Marriage and Civil Partnership (Amendment) Bill 2016 alongside consideration of the Equality Bill 2016.
